corpus_policy.supersedes_note: Three corrections, all COUNSEL's, recorded rather than quietly rewritten. v1.0 refused a restricted file outright in every context: that read a reproduction-and-transmission reservation as a bar on private reading, which it is not. v1.1 defaulted the whole pool to REFUSE on an undeclared licence: that ignored SA-2, under which the operator's declaration of the acquisition channel is evidence, and SA-001, which already settled that publisher newsletter distribution is publication by the publisher. v1.2 still treated any served index touching WEF as restricted: that conflated CITING a published figure with REPUBLISHING the publication. Quoting figures with attribution, and computing and reporting derived statistics, is accepted and expected academic use and needs no permission. What a reservation actually reaches is substantial verbatim reproduction. The scopes below say so.

academic_citation.what_it_is: Citing a published figure with attribution, and computing, reporting and publishing statistics derived from it. Covers the index, the served MCP surface, the dashboard, the paper and any public artefact that references a source rather than reproducing it.
academic_citation.default_reason: This is the normal scholarly use of a published source and it requires no permission from the publisher. Attribution is the obligation, not consent. An instrument built to be checked by reviewers must be able to cite what it was checked against.

private_analysis.what_it_is: A corpus held on the operator's own machine and queried only by him or by agents acting for him. Nothing leaves the machine.
private_analysis.default_reason: Reading a document one lawfully holds is not reproduction or transmission, and indexing it for one's own retrieval is reading with a machine.

served_verbatim.what_it_is: Serving substantial verbatim text or reproducing a source's tables to a third party: a public retrieval index that returns source passages, a republished ranking table, a redistributed PDF.
served_verbatim.default_reason: This is the one thing a redistribution reservation actually reaches. It is also the only scope where the publisher's terms and this ecosystem's interest can diverge, so it is the only one that needs a gate.

corpus_policy.rule: Scope decides, and only one scope restricts anything. Citing a figure is not reproducing a publication, and holding a file is not transmitting it. What a reservation reaches is handing substantial verbatim text onward, so that is what served_verbatim guards and nothing else is gated.

sources.reason: OFFICIAL source. Cite its figures freely with attribution and publish statistics derived from them: that is accepted and expected academic use. Hold and index it privately. Do not republish the ranking tables or serve substantial verbatim passages, which is the one act the reservation reaches.

Explicit local quarantine marking. Refused in both scopes on the name, so a file can be pulled out of circulation without a register round trip. This is the one pattern that overrides the pool declaration.

pool_declaration.statement: The material in this pool was received from its publishers through their own newsletter, marketing and SEO distribution. The operator did not circumvent a control, breach a term or pay. Under SA-2 that testimony is evidence, and under SA-001's reasoning distribution to a list the publisher invited the public to join is an act of publication by the publisher.
pool_declaration.effect: Every file in this pool is ADMITTED to academic_citation and private_analysis unless it carries the _RESTRICTED_ quarantine marking. served_verbatim stays decided per source.
pool_declaration.why_this_is_not_a_blanket_waiver: It settles possession and use, which is what the acquisition channel is for. It does not overwrite an explicit stated term, and SA-001 already says so: raw redistribution follows the publisher's stated terms. That is why WEF and Forrester still fail served_retrieval while passing private_analysis.
pool_declaration.default_tier_reason: A file with no enumerated entry arrived through the pool and is practice material by default. Promoting a source to OFFICIAL is an operator act and is recorded per source, never inferred from the folder it sits in.

corpus_policy.precedence: A _RESTRICTED_ marking wins over everything. Otherwise the first matching source entry decides, and a file matching no entry falls to the scope default: ADMIT for private_analysis under the pool declaration, REFUSE for served_retrieval.

OFFICIAL.what_it_is: A source of record. Its figures may be cited as evidence in the index, the served surface and the paper, and its vintage is tracked so a new edition is a scheduled event rather than a surprise.
OFFICIAL.obligation: Carries a vintage in this manifest. A new edition is a change to check against, not a file to drop in the folder.

COMPLEMENTARY.what_it_is: Practice and operations material. It informs how the ecosystem is built and run. It is never cited as evidence for a measurement or a finding.
publishers: vendor, analyst and practitioner publications received through publisher newsletter and marketing distribution
COMPLEMENTARY.obligation: May shape a design decision. May not support a claim about the world. The Forrester action gap framework is the worked example: the framework is applied, the report is not cited as evidence.

source_tiers.why_the_tier_is_not_a_licence: Tier is epistemic standing inside this ecosystem. It is assigned by the operator and it governs what a source may be used FOR. Licence is assigned by the publisher and governs what may be handed onward. Designating the World Economic Forum an official source does not license republication of its tables, which is why SA-006 still refuses served_retrieval while admitting private_analysis and while the ETI figures are cited freely as derived aggregates. The two fields answer different questions and neither overrides the other.
